resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the present groundhouse was built in 1963; firelookout.com says the present ground cab was built in 1952. Both are reported; the record's 1952 comes from firelookout.com. No third source read settles it.
NHLR says a 70-foot steel tower replaced the 1930 platform; firelookout.com says 72 feet with a tent cabin. The story reports both.
NHLR gives 6,723 ft (2,049 m); firelookout.com gives 6,810 ft. The brief's 2049.2 m matches NHLR.

notes_for_editor: Core facts agree across sources: Granite County location, DNRC Forestry Division administration since 1973, NHLR registration March 31, 2003, standing status. The date of the present cab is in dispute (1952 per firelookout.com, 1963 per NHLR); the story reports both and the editor should choose how the record shows it. The brief's height_m 21.9 looks like the former 72-foot tower, so a correction is proposed. The marker database text repeats NHLR wording, so it is used only for the road access sentence. A search snippet dates a Forest Service photo in the Montana History Portal (mtmemory.org node 20375) to 1952; it does not say which structure is pictured, so it is not cited. FFLA credits photos to the Montana Memory Project and Gary Weber, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos added. The staffing as_of date is the access date because the firelookout.com page is undated. Not verified: whether the public can climb or stay in the cab, and current condition.
